title: Read a difference
summary: A diff shows how current content differs from another version. Review it before saving the next version.
introduction: A diff shows how current content differs from another version. Review it before saving the next version. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A diff shows how current content differs from another version. Review it before saving the next version.

blocks.code:
printf "A second line
" >> note.txt
git diff
blocks.title: Read a difference

blocks.text: The difference shows the added second line. Lines with a plus are additions in the displayed comparison.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Stage the change and compare git diff with git diff --cached.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: An empty unstaged diff does not prove there are no staged changes.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).

seo.title: Git: Read a difference
seo.description: Learn about read a difference in Git. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
